title: Chewy Boiled New York Bagels with Cream Cheese
summary: A stiff honey-sweetened bread-flour dough is shaped into 8 rings, retarded in the fridge 12-24 hours, boiled 45 seconds a side and baked hot until glossy.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: about 1 tbsp; for colour; very little clings to the bagels

ingredients.item: fine cornmeal or semolina, for the tray

steps.title: Mix and knead
steps.text: Dissolve the honey in the ice-cold water, mix with the flour, yeast and salt, rest 10 minutes, then knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and very firm.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Cut into 8 pieces, roll into taut balls and rest 15 minutes.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll into 25 cm ropes, wrap round your hand with the ends overlapping and roll the join to seal. Set on the cornmeal-dusted tray.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230 °C (210 °C fan). Boil the bagels 45 seconds per side in water with honey and drain briefly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 18-22 minutes until glossy and deep golden. Cool 15 minutes, then split and spread with cream cheese.

tips: The dough should be stiff; resist adding water.
Seal the join firmly or the rings open in the pot.
A bagel that floats within a few seconds is ready to boil.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
